newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs soar in Tokyo on unexpected "tankan" results.
newsitem.headline: JGBs soar in Tokyo on unexpected "tankan" results.

text.p: Long-term yen cash bonds and futures soared by late Wednesday trade on the unexpectedly weak results of the Bank of Japan's quarterly "tankan" survey.
"The survey forced many participants to dump their previous scenarios about the economic recovery," said Yorinobu Hara, senior deputy general manager at Asahi Securities Co.

The BOJ's survey of corporate sentiment showed its key diffusion index for big manufacturers dropped to minus seven from minus three in the previous survey in May, in contrast to earlier market expectations of a small improvement.

Before the survey, there was a view the BOJ may refrain from tightening the current super-easy credit this calendar year. But many operators now believe the BOJ may not raise interest rates until the end of this fiscal year, traders said.
Key December 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended at 120.39, up 1.14 from Tuesday's close.

Asahi Securities' Hara said: "The key contract's consistent rise above 120 means there is a growing view that the BOJ cannot change its assessment on the economy for about a year from now after the bank sees the effects from a planned rise in consumption tax to five percent (from April 1)."
The key contract moved in a wide range of between 119.06 and 120.54 in turnover of a hectic 78,275 contracts.

Earlier in the morning, there was talk the key diffusion index might be near the top end of expectations at plus five. But those who had sold on such talk were forced to buy what was offered in the cash market after the tankan was released at 0200 GMT before the futures market reopened at 0330 GMT.

"Apart from minus seven for the key diffusion index, it made a big impression, seeing the index forecast to improve only to zero in December," said Tadao Takashima, assistant general manager of bond trading at Daiwa Securities Co.
Another rally was later triggered by a senior BOJ official's bearish comments on capital spending, traders said.

The tankan showed an upward revision in companies' capital investment plans. But Masayuki Matsushima, director of the BOJ's Research and Statistics Department, said that due to the slowness in the microchip market "there is still a possibility companies may consider cutting down their capital spending."

In the cash market, the yield of the key 182nd 10-year JGBs briefly fell below three percent for the first time since February 14. The yield stood at 3.020 percent at 0742 GMT, down from Tuesday's 3.145 percent.

"It seems that the economic recovery is now what it was six months ago," Daiwa's Sakashima said. "But we have to remember economic conditions are fundamentally different from those of last year. Thus, the rally may be curbed before the key bond yield falls to this year's low of 2.90 percent."

The yield of the benchmark 10-year JGBs had been above 3.00 percent since February 15, when Finance Minister Wataru Kubo spoke of the unfavourable effect low interest rates have on pensioners, putting bond traders, who did not expect a rate rise soon, on their guard, traders said.
